title: First-touch attribution poisoning: unauthenticated /auth/oauth/google persist attacker-chosen UTM params into a signed cookie, locked into the victim's $set_once on their first Google signup
detail: The public GET initiate route persists attacker-chosen query values into a signed cookie on any cross-site top-level navigation (SameSite=Lax permits the Set-Cookie). The callback then writes them as write-once $set_once person properties, permanently attributing the victim's first Google signup to an attacker-controlled campaign/click-id. Impact is attribution corruption only: values are allow-listed, clamped (200 chars), percent-encoded, and signature-verified, so no injection or forgery. The same poisoning class pre-exists via crafted landing URLs on the password path (#466), but this endpoint is a new persistence surface needing no SPA or landing page — one link click plus Google's continue.
recommended_fix: Accept and document as inherent to URL-param attribution, or require a first-party signal on initiate (e.g. Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin or same-origin referer) before persisting params, so only SPA-originated initiates write the cookie.
